## 油輪開始通過荷姆茲海峽，美債漲勢延伸至長端

週四油輪開始通過荷姆茲海峽，投資人也在Fed偏鷹決議後買進中長天期美債。5年期殖利率下降4個基點至4.23%，10及30年期各下降3個基點，分別收在4.46%與4.90%。2年期僅下降1個基點至4.19%，幾乎保留了週三15個基點的升幅。

載有近1,000萬桶原油的船隻已進出海峽，讓美伊協議承諾的恢復通行，開始轉化為實際的供應變化，儘管規模仍有限。10年期損益兩平通膨率再降1個基點至2.25%。股市上漲、波動率下降，顯示美債買盤並非來自全面避險。$240億5年期TIPS續發也獲得強勁認購，投資人願意在較高實質殖利率買進債券。

Fed政策轉向的影響仍留在前端。Kevin Warsh首次主持會議前，短期利率市場幾乎不認為7月會升息；會後機率接近50%，10月前升息1碼也已完整反映。初領失業救濟金人數維持偏低，區域製造業調查反彈，沒有給市場足夠理由忽略Fed的通膨疑慮。美國以外，英國央行在表決分歧下維持利率，印尼與菲律賓則升息。能源成本下降緩解了一項債市壓力，各國政策反應卻並不相同。

## TIPS標售需求強，工廠成本仍在上升

2年與10年期、2年與30年期美債利差各收窄2個基點，分別至27及71個基點。5年期領漲，使2s5s10s蝶式利差下降4個基點至−19個基點，2s10s30s下降2個基點至−17個基點。週三前端大跌後，買盤先回到中段，卻尚未撤銷對Fed升息的定價。

一週以來，2年期殖利率仍上升14個基點，5年期上升5個基點，10年期上升1個基點，30年期則下降5個基點。一個月來，2年期上升12個基點，30年期下降24個基點。Fed會議之後，短期利率預期與長端表現的差距，反而比之前更大。

10年期名目殖利率下降，實質殖利率與通膨補償均有貢獻。10年期TIPS殖利率下降2個基點至2.21%，損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點。5年期實質殖利率維持1.96%；7、20及30年期分別下降2、3及3個基點，至2.07%、2.52%與2.70%。投資人降低長期通膨溢價，但對政策較敏感的5年期實質殖利率並未跟著下降。

週四早間的美國數據，仍使Fed難以宣告通膨風險已過。初領失業救濟金人數由修正後的23萬降至22.6萬，接近預估的22.5萬。不過，續領人數增加2.4萬至181萬，初領人數4週平均也由21.925萬升至22.325萬。費城Fed製造業指數由−0.4反彈至10.3，新訂單27.3、就業7.9，支付價格則從47.9升至53.2。勞動市場局部放緩，工廠活動與投入成本卻更強。

5年期TIPS在遠高於4月的實質殖利率水準，仍取得充足買盤。財政部續發$240億，得標殖利率1.955%，4月新券發行時則為1.367%。投標倍數由2.57升至2.61；間接投標人獲配68.59%，直接投標人27.99%，交易商僅承接3.43%，低於前次8.48%。資料缺少同時點的發行前交易報價，能直接比較的是投標與獲配情況。標售結果也與5年期實質殖利率收盤持平相符。

國庫券標售較不平均。$700億4週國庫券得標利率3.580%，投標倍數從3.13降至2.99，但間接投標比重升至72.30%，交易商承接24.46%。$750億8週國庫券得標利率3.640%，投標倍數從2.94降至2.57，間接投標比重降至51.49%，交易商承接44.56%。次級市場短券殖利率有漲有跌：8週上升3個基點至3.72%，13週下降2個基點至3.75%。8週標售偏弱較值得注意，極短天期現金利率並未全面急升。

## 混合資本獲認購，弱勢借款人付出更高成本

NextEra Energy的3券次發債，使其成為全球最大的混合債發行人。今年主要貨幣計價的混合債發行量已逾$730億，接近2023年同期的5倍。NextEra一筆40年期、發行20年後才首次可贖回的債券，在3個券次中吸引最多訂單；另外2個券次也成為本週交易最活絡的美國公司債。投資人願意承擔極長的存續及延期風險以換取收益，儘管混合債相對廣泛投資級債的溢價已收窄至56個基點，接近歷史低點。

這類債券讓公用事業為電網擴張及資料中心用電籌資，同時取得評級機構部分權益資本認列。債權人則須接受較低清償順位、可能遞延付息，以及何時贖回的不確定性。NextEra的強勁訂單，顯示市場認同的是這筆交易所提供的風險與收益組合。

SpaceX帶來規模更大的潛在供給。銀行正在籌備公司IPO後首筆投資級美元債，規模至少$200億，部分將用於再融資2027年9月到期的$200億短期過橋貸款，其餘支持投資計畫。3大評級機構在週四稍晚給予債券投資級評級，但發行尚未啟動。一項外部模型預測，公司淨負債可能從近期約$130億升至2031年逾$4,000億；那是未來融資規模的預估，並非目前已發生的債務。

4家最大AI投資企業規劃2026年資本支出最高達$7,250億。Alphabet第1季近10年來首次未買回股票，一年前同期回購金額超過$150億；另有一家大型發行人計畫籌措約$850億新股資金。減少回購可以保留投資能力，但在計畫報酬尚未確立前，龐大支出仍可能要求企業反覆發債或發股。

弱勢借款人取得認購，則須提供更高收益或讓步。Shutterfly在一部分高收益再融資交易提供12.5%殖利率；Apollo把持有的第二順位債權轉入新的$2.5億次順位券次，清償順位隨之下降。Shutterfly在3月底有$24億債務，現金流又高度集中在第4季。第1季EBITDA虧損由一年前$1,720萬擴大至$1,970萬，但調整後EBITDA由虧損$150萬改善為約$40萬；營收下降8%至$3.135億。公司流動性為$4.74億，循環額度尚未動用。

新發行的$11.5億高收益債獲超額認購，價格定於面額的98.2%，之後在次級市場上漲。這對Shutterfly的再融資是正面結果；穆迪仍估計，困境債務交換約有四分之一最終走向破產或漏付。評級B3的Eolo則仍與Apollo深入磋商約€5億私募貸款，準備替換2028年到期的€3.75億債券及€1.4億循環貸款；其債券報價約為面額的86%。協商尚未完成，折價也反映投資人對既有債權的評價。

銀行為出售軟體公司貸款，同樣提供大幅折讓。蒙特婁銀行領銜的團隊持有Pellera Technologies收購貸款逾1年後，推介$7.75億債權，利差為基準利率加450個基點，價格低至面額的92%。Pretium則描述有實體房地產抵押貸款的另一類需求：利差為SOFR加600至650個基點，目標槓桿後報酬率為十幾%。面臨AI改變軟體市場的借款人，與有具體不動產擔保的放款人，所面對的投資需求與價格已明顯不同。

Braskem的展延方案則遭債權人反對。提議包含延長到期日、降低票息與寬限期，但沒有注入新資本，也不安排債轉股。短天期債券的待遇優於較長期貸款，貸款人質疑擔保與股東支持是否足夠。若無法取得必要同意，公司可能尋求法院保護。爭議不只是到期時間，還包括各類債權人如何分配價值。

市政基礎設施也增加了債券供給。今年美國供水與汙水處理借款人發債逾$210億，可比發行速度至少是2015年以來最快。老舊設施、監管要求與氣候韌性需求增加，聯邦循環基金支持又可能減少。伊利諾州今年已發行逾$9.4億，2025年超過$10億，2021年則約$1,600萬。這些債券支持必要服務，但營建成本上升與公共資金缺口，也讓更多長天期供給進入市政債投資組合。

信用ETF隨股市及美債上漲，LQD漲0.28%，HYG漲0.35%，JNK漲0.34%。整體氣氛改善，但個別交易的價格仍顯示，借款人品質、清償順位及擔保條件，會決定實際融資成本。

## 英國選擇觀望，亞洲央行升息步調各異

英國央行以7票對2票維持利率3.75%，Megan Greene與Huw Pill主張立即升至4%。多數委員認為，需求偏弱、勞動市場轉鬆，加上4月GDP下降0.1%，允許先觀察。油價下跌使央行將預估通膨高點由3.6%降至3.25%，目前通膨為2.8%。市場仍完整反映今年再升息一次，英鎊則兌美元貶約0.5%。

ECB已將存款利率升至2.25%。首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，中性利率估計區間的上緣已升至2.5%，因此再升息一次，也未必代表政策明顯緊縮；他形容能源衝擊規模中等且具持續性。Jose Luis Escrivá說，較高能源成本已反映在服務、運輸與食品價格，但工資的後續傳導尚未出現。西班牙央行將2026年通膨預測上調至3.6%，成長預測維持2.3%。

台灣連續第9季維持基準利率2%，但政策語氣偏鷹。央行受惠於AI出口與民間投資強勁，將2026年成長預測由7.28%上修至9.45%，通膨預測為1.91%。股市上漲60%，也引發信貸過度擴張的疑慮。在銀行流動性原已偏緊的情況下，這次未升息避免立即增加壓力，較強的成長前景仍使日後升息成為可能。

日本本週升息後，日圓仍偏弱，一度跌至每$1兌¥160.80；隔夜交換反映年底前再升息機率約80%。日本當局4月28日至5月27日已花費創紀錄的¥11.73兆干預，投機性日圓空單又接近9年高點，使投資人警覺匯市干預或利差交易突然平倉。美國固定收益市場收盤後，東京公布5月核心通膨維持1.4%，不含生鮮食品與能源的指標為1.8%；能源補貼使汽油價格較一年前低7%。這些後續數據應進入下一個亞洲交易時段的判斷。

中國的國內融資愈來愈依靠債券。5月債券占未償還信用總額的比重創紀錄達30%，債市規模約人民幣200兆元。前5個月新企業債融資增加人民幣1.7兆元，比上年同期多逾80%，新貸款則減少11%。人民銀行流動性支持及貸款需求偏弱，使5年期政府債殖利率降至1.5%，低於5年期貸款市場報價利率3.5%。人民幣10兆元地方政府債務置換，則在融資成本下降的同時，增加了可交易債券供給。

香港規劃中的5年期中國國債期貨，可能讓境外投資人更容易對沖這個日益擴大的市場。合資格外國機構也取得境內期貨市場准入，新回購機制則允許外國央行及主權基金以中國公債融資。不過，香港期貨合約仍待推出與形成流動性，週四尚未產生新的現券需求。

## 印尼與菲律賓升息，巴西降息空間受到檢驗

印尼央行將政策利率上調25個基點至5.75%，約一個月內第3次升息，2026年累計升息100個基點。印尼盾由貶轉升，收盤上漲0.2%，但10年期政府債殖利率上升15個基點，股市下跌。從7月起，購買至少$1萬外幣須提供實際交易依據，門檻由原先$10萬下調。利率與匯率措施顯示，對抗輸入性通膨與強勢美元須付出代價。

菲律賓也將附買回利率提高25個基點至4.75%，理由是核心通膨壓力擴散，可能產生進一步傳導。決策符合多數預期，但一些投資人原本期待更大幅度升息，披索因此下跌0.3%。官員保留後續行動空間，卻沒有暗示傾向大幅升息。兩國都收緊政策，市場給予的反應並不相同。

巴西前一日晚間降息後，雷亞爾轉弱、長天期交換利率上升。匯率貶約1.3%，交換利率升約20個基點。全年通膨已加速至4.72%，高於3%目標，央行並將2027年底通膨預測上調至3.7%。把達標時程延至2028年初，使Selic得以下降至14.25%，投資人卻已開始質疑降息還能持續多久。

其他本地市場受不同買盤支撐。馬來西亞10年期政府債殖利率為3.58%，低於可比的令吉交換利率3.70%，債券與交換利率差為正12個基點，而數個區域市場的利差為負。35億令吉、2040年到期的伊斯蘭債，投標倍數達3.41。政府可能無法達到赤字占GDP 3.5%的目標，但穩定的國內需求及石油淨出口國地位，限制了供給壓力反映在殖利率上的幅度。

Pimco基金5月淨買進6.7兆哥倫比亞披索政府債，約合$20億，現持有外國投資人總計$430億部位中的約30%。本地債券一個月漲逾11%，10年期殖利率較5月高點下降約2.5個百分點至12%以下。買盤降低了再融資成本，但總統決選前，市場也更容易受單一大型投資人部位變動影響。

印度6月5日取消部分政府債券的稅負與持有上限後，指數合格券吸引3,263億盧比、約$35億資金。德勤估計，稅務變更可能使外國投資人的報酬提高15%至20%。由於合格債券數量也增加，不能把所有流入都歸功於稅負減輕。稅後收益改善與限制放寬，讓印度不同於主要靠防禦性升息留住資金的市場。

俄羅斯的國內融資難題來自財政支出，而非迫在眉睫的外債到期。制裁使海外市場大致關閉，國防支出預估超出原預算4兆至5兆盧布，約$550億至$690億。前5個月赤字達6兆盧布、占GDP 2.6%，比全年目標高約60%；2026年債務上限也已達到。彭博經濟研究估計，未來10年利息支出至少占GDP 15%，大約等於目前公債餘額占GDP的比重。在被迫仰賴昂貴國內資金時，初始負債率低帶來的保障有限。

即使美元走強，EMB仍上漲0.47%。同一天印尼公債殖利率上升、菲律賓披索貶值、巴西市場對降息反應負面，各國結果遠比基金漲幅分歧。

## 油輪恢復通行，各類資產走勢仍有差異

WTI微跌0.25%至$76.60，布蘭特微升0.38%至$79.85；一週以來兩者仍分別下跌12.67%及11.65%。科威特計畫一週內將產量提高至每日200萬桶以上。載有近1,000萬桶原油的船隻已進出荷姆茲海峽，但受損設施及先前滯留的貨量，仍限制供應恢復速度。對美債通膨預期而言，實際通行的消息比當天兩種原油小幅且方向不同的價格變化更有意義。

S&P 500上漲1.08%，Nasdaq 100上漲2.48%，半導體股大漲6.42%；VIX下跌11.06%至16.40。能源成本可望下降，加上科技業持續投資，帶動股市走強。同一波投資，也將帶來更多企業債與公用事業基礎設施融資需求。

美元指數上漲0.76%至100.85，延續Fed預測公布後的走勢。黃金下跌3.09%至$4,224.10，預期短期利率上升與眼前地緣政治疑慮減輕，都可能降低持有黃金的吸引力。股市與美元可以同時走強：前者受惠能源緩和，後者仍反映較高的美國政策利率路徑。

## 休市後，數據與債券供給密集登場

美國固定收益市場將因六月節於6月19日休市。6月22日恢復交易，當天有$890億13週與$770億26週國庫券供給。財政部接著於23日發行$690億2年期、24日發行$700億5年期、25日發行$440億7年期公債。更大的標售規模到來時，買盤能否延續週四TIPS標售的強勢，將更容易看清。

個人所得與支出報告於6月25日公布，市場預估整體PCE物價月增0.5%、核心月增0.3%。當天早上還有失業救濟金、耐久財訂單及GDP修正值。Warsh首次主持Fed會議後，這些數據將幫助投資人判斷，現貨能源回落是否已反映在實際物價，而需求是否仍強。

中國6月22日公布貸款市場報價利率，加拿大當天公布5月CPI，澳洲6月24日公布月度CPI。市場預期中國1年及5年期LPR分別維持3.00%與3.50%；加拿大調整權重後的物價指數，預期顯示整體通膨由2.8%升至3.0%。澳洲上次月增與年增讀數分別為0.4%及4.2%。這些數據將呈現美國以外能源價格如何傳導至物價。

哥倫比亞6月21日舉行總統決選，墨西哥央行則於25日決策，預期維持6.50%。相比EMB整體表現，披索與哥倫比亞債市的反應，更能反映兩地各自的政策及財政風險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil Tankers Cross Hormuz as Treasuries Recover Beyond the Front End

Treasuries rose on Thursday as oil shipments began moving through the Strait of Hormuz and investors bought intermediate and long maturities after the Federal Reserve's hawkish turn. The 5-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.23%; the 10- and 30-year each declined 3, to 4.46% and 4.90%. The 2-year slipped just 1 basis point to 4.19%, retaining almost all of Wednesday's 15-basis-point increase.

Ships carrying nearly 10 million barrels of oil had emerged from or entered the strait, turning the US-Iran agreement's promise of renewed passage into a physical, if still partial, change in supply. The 10-year breakeven inflation rate edged down another basis point to 2.25%. Equities climbed and volatility fell, so the Treasury bid did not depend on a flight from risk. A well-supported $24 billion 5-year TIPS reopening gave investors another way to express demand for duration at higher real yields.

The Fed's policy shift remained visible. Short-rate markets moved from virtually no chance of a July increase before Kevin Warsh's debut toward odds approaching one-half afterward, with a full quarter-point increase priced by October. Initial jobless claims were low and a regional factory survey rebounded, offering little reason to dismiss the inflation concerns behind the projections. Outside the US, the Bank of England held in a split vote while Indonesia and the Philippines raised rates. Falling energy costs were easing one pressure on bonds, but the policy response differed sharply by country.

## A Strong TIPS Sale Meets Firm Factory Costs

The 2s10s and 2s30s Treasury slopes each narrowed 2 basis points, to 27 and 71. The 5-year led the day's rally, taking the 2s5s10s butterfly down 4 basis points to -19; 2s10s30s fell 2 to -17. After Wednesday's front-end selloff, buyers returned first to the belly rather than pricing an immediate reversal of Fed tightening.

Over a week, the 2-year yield was still 14 basis points higher, the 5-year up 5 and the 10-year up 1, while the 30-year was 5 lower. Over a month, the 2-year remained 12 basis points higher and the 30-year was 24 lower. The distance between short-rate expectations and long-duration performance had widened, rather than closed, since the Fed meeting.

Both real yields and breakevens contributed to the 10-year nominal gain. The 10-year TIPS yield fell 2 basis points to 2.21% and the breakeven eased 1 basis point. The 5-year real yield held at 1.96%, while 7-, 20- and 30-year real yields dropped 2, 3 and 3 basis points, to 2.07%, 2.52% and 2.70%. Investors accepted a lower long-term inflation premium without meaningfully lowering the policy-sensitive 5-year real yield.

The morning's US data kept pressure on the Fed to wait before declaring victory. Initial jobless claims fell to 226,000 from a revised 230,000, close to the 225,000 forecast. Continuing claims rose 24,000 to 1.810 million, however, and the four-week initial-claims average climbed to 223,250 from 219,250. The Philadelphia Fed index rebounded to 10.3 from -0.4; new orders reached 27.3 and employment 7.9, while prices paid rose to 53.2 from 47.9. Hiring conditions showed some softening around the edges, but activity and input costs were firmer.

The 5-year TIPS reopening drew substantial demand at a real yield far higher than in April. Treasury sold $24 billion at 1.955%, versus 1.367% at the earlier new issue. Bid-to-cover improved to 2.61 from 2.57; indirect bidders took 68.59% and direct bidders 27.99%, leaving dealers just 3.43%, down from 8.48%. Without a contemporaneous when-issued quote, participation and allocation are the available measures of demand. The auction was consistent with the 5-year real yield's unchanged finish.

Bill auctions were less even. The $70 billion 4-week sale cleared at 3.580%, with cover of 2.99 versus 3.13 previously. Its indirect share nevertheless rose to 72.30%, and dealers took 24.46%. The $75 billion 8-week sale stopped at 3.640%; cover fell to 2.57 from 2.94, indirect awards declined to 51.49% and dealers received 44.56%. Short bill yields moved in both directions, with the 8-week up 3 basis points to 3.72% and the 13-week down 2 to 3.75%. The weaker 8-week sale stood out, but there was no common surge in short cash yields.

## Hybrids Draw Buyers; Stressed Borrowers Pay Up

NextEra Energy's three-tranche sale made it the world's largest issuer of hybrid bonds. Major-currency hybrid issuance has exceeded $73 billion this year, almost five times the comparable 2023 volume. A 40-year security with no first call for 20 years attracted the most bids among NextEra's tranches, and two of its bonds became the week's most actively traded US corporate issues. The extra income drew buyers even as the hybrid premium over broad investment grade narrowed to 56 basis points, near a record low.

The instruments let a utility raise capital for grid expansion and data-center power demand while receiving some equity treatment from rating agencies. Bondholders, in turn, accept subordination, possible coupon deferral and uncertainty about when a bond will be redeemed. The strong order book showed appetite for that combination of income and risk at NextEra's terms.

SpaceX posed a larger prospective supply question. Bankers were preparing its first investment-grade dollar bond offering of at least $20 billion following its IPO, partly to refinance a temporary $20 billion bridge loan due in September 2027 and partly to fund investment. All three major rating firms assigned investment-grade bond scores late Thursday. The sale had not yet been launched. An external model projected net debt above $400 billion by 2031 from roughly $13 billion recently, illustrating the scale of financing that one future AI and data-center capital program might require; that projection was not an outstanding debt figure.

The four biggest AI spenders planned as much as $725 billion of capital expenditure for 2026. Alphabet made no share repurchases in the first quarter for the first time in almost a decade, after buying back more than $15 billion a year earlier; another large issuer planned roughly $85 billion of new equity. Less cash devoted to buybacks can preserve capacity to invest, but large capital programs may still require repeat debt or equity issuance before their returns are established.

At weaker borrowers, investor demand came with much steeper terms. Shutterfly offered a 12.5% yield on a high-yield portion of its refinancing. Apollo rolled a second-lien holding into a new $250 million junior tranche, moving lower in the repayment order. Shutterfly had $2.4 billion of debt at the end of March, with its cash generation concentrated in the fourth quarter. Its first-quarter EBITDA loss widened to $19.7 million from $17.2 million a year earlier, although adjusted EBITDA improved to roughly $400,000 from an adjusted loss of $1.5 million. Revenue fell 8% to $313.5 million; liquidity was $474 million, with a revolver undrawn.

The issuer's $1.15 billion of new junk bonds were oversubscribed, priced at 98.2 and then traded higher. That response was encouraging for this refinancing, though Moody's estimates roughly one-quarter of distressed exchanges later lead to bankruptcy or a missed payment. Eolo, rated B3, was still in advanced talks with Apollo for about €500 million of private debt to replace €375 million of bonds and a €140 million revolver due in 2028; its bonds were quoted near 86% of face value. Negotiation is not completion, and the discount showed the cost investors still assigned to the existing claims.

Banks were also offering large concessions to move a software loan. A Bank of Montreal-led group marketed $775 million of Pellera Technologies buyout debt at a spread of 450 basis points and as low as 92 cents on the dollar after holding it for more than a year. Pretium described a different source of demand in loans backed by physical property: it charged SOFR plus 600-650 basis points and targeted returns in the mid-teens after leverage. Borrowers exposed to AI-driven software change and lenders with tangible collateral were finding distinct markets, each with its own price.

Braskem's proposed maturity extension faced resistance from creditors. It offered longer maturities, lower coupons and grace periods, without a fresh capital injection or debt-for-equity exchange. Shorter bonds received better proposed treatment than longer facilities, and lenders questioned collateral and shareholder support. Failure to gather enough backing could lead to court protection. The available financing problem was as much about how value would be divided as about the calendar of maturities.

Municipal infrastructure brought another supply channel. US water and sewer borrowers have issued more than $21 billion this year, the fastest comparable pace since at least 2015, as aging systems, regulation and climate resilience needs coincide with the possibility of less federal revolving-fund support. Illinois alone has sold more than $940 million after issuing over $1 billion in 2025, compared with about $16 million in 2021. These bonds finance essential services, while rising construction costs and public-funding gaps are moving more duration into municipal portfolios.

Credit funds rose with stocks and Treasuries: LQD gained 0.28%, HYG 0.35% and JNK 0.34%. The gain captured the improved mood, while individual transaction prices showed how much financing still depends on borrower quality, ranking and collateral.

## Britain Waits; Asia's Central Banks Tighten at Different Speeds

The Bank of England held at 3.75% by a 7-2 vote. Megan Greene and Huw Pill wanted an immediate increase to 4%, but weaker demand, a looser labor market and a 0.1% fall in April GDP gave the majority room to wait. Lower oil led the bank to reduce its expected inflation peak to 3.25% from 3.6%, against current inflation of 2.8%. Another increase remained fully priced for the year, and sterling was about 0.5% weaker against the dollar.

The ECB had already raised its deposit rate to 2.25%. Chief Economist Philip Lane said the upper end of estimates for the neutral rate had moved to 2.5%, so one further increase need not make policy plainly restrictive. He described the energy shock as medium-sized and persistent. Jose Luis Escrivá said higher energy costs were appearing in services, transport and food, although wage pass-through had not yet materialized. Spain's central bank lifted its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.6% while retaining a 2.3% growth projection.

Taiwan held its benchmark at 2% for a ninth consecutive quarter but struck a hawkish tone. Its central bank raised the 2026 growth forecast from 7.28% to 9.45% on strong AI exports and private investment and projected 1.91% consumer inflation. A 60% equity rally raised concern about excessive credit expansion. With bank liquidity already tight, the hold avoided further immediate pressure, while the faster growth outlook kept a later increase in view.

The yen remained weak after Japan's rate increase earlier in the week, trading as low as 160.80 per dollar. Overnight swaps put the chance of another move by year-end at about 80%. Japanese authorities had spent a record ¥11.73 trillion between April 28 and May 27, and speculative short-yen positions were near a nine-year high. That history left investors alert to intervention or a sudden unwind of currency-funded positions. May inflation figures released in Tokyo after US fixed-income trading ended showed core at 1.4% and the measure excluding fresh food and energy at 1.8%; energy subsidies kept gasoline prices 7% below a year earlier. The later data inform the next Asian session, not Thursday's completed US close.

China's bond market was doing more of the work of domestic financing. Bonds accounted for a record 30% of credit outstanding in May in a market of about 200 trillion yuan. New corporate-bond financing rose 1.7 trillion yuan in the first five months, more than 80% above a year earlier, while new loans fell 11%. PBOC liquidity and weak loan demand pushed the 5-year government yield to 1.5%, against a 3.5% 5-year loan prime rate. A 10-trillion-yuan local-government debt swap is adding marketable supply even as cheaper bonds ease financing costs.

Hong Kong's planned 5-year Chinese government-bond futures could give offshore investors a way to hedge that growing market. Qualified foreign institutions also gained access to onshore futures, and new repo facilities allow foreign central banks and sovereign funds to finance Chinese bonds. The proposed Hong Kong contract still needed a launch and active trading; it had not created new cash demand on Thursday.

## Indonesia and the Philippines Raise Rates; Brazil Tests Its Easing Room

Bank Indonesia lifted its policy rate 25 basis points to 5.75%, its third increase in about a month and a cumulative 100 basis points of tightening in 2026. The rupiah reversed losses to finish 0.2% stronger, while 10-year government yields rose 15 basis points and stocks fell. From July, foreign-currency purchases of at least $10,000 will require an underlying transaction, down from a $100,000 threshold. The rate and currency measures showed the cost of defending against imported inflation and a stronger dollar.

The Philippines also raised its reverse-repurchase rate 25 basis points, to 4.75%, citing broader core inflation and the risk of second-round effects. The decision matched the majority forecast, but the peso slipped 0.3% as some investors had expected a larger step. Officials left room for further action without indicating a preference for a sharp increase. Both central banks tightened; the market did not reward them equally.

Brazil's cut the previous evening was followed by a weaker real and higher long-dated swaps. The currency fell about 1.3%, while swaps rose roughly 20 basis points. Annual inflation had accelerated to 4.72% against a 3% target, and the central bank raised its late-2027 forecast to 3.7%. Extending the target horizon to early 2028 allowed it to lower the Selic rate to 14.25%, but investors were already questioning how long easing could continue.

Other local markets benefited from different buyer bases. Malaysia's 10-year government yield was 3.58%, below the comparable 3.70% ringgit swap rate, a positive bond-swap spread of 12 basis points even as several regional peers traded negative. A 3.5 billion-ringgit sale of 2040 Islamic securities drew bids equal to 3.41 times the amount offered. The government may miss its 3.5%-of-GDP deficit target; domestic demand and its position as a net oil exporter have nevertheless limited the supply premium.

Pimco funds bought a net 6.7 trillion Colombian pesos of government bonds in May, about $2 billion, and now hold roughly 30% of the $43 billion owned by foreign investors. Local bonds gained more than 11% over the past month, with 10-year yields down about 2.5 percentage points from their May high to below 12%. The rally has lowered refinancing costs while leaving the market sensitive to one large investor's positioning ahead of a presidential runoff.

India's June 5 changes to taxes and ownership limits on selected government bonds helped bring 326.3 billion rupees, or $3.5 billion, into index-eligible securities. Deloitte estimated that the tax change could lift foreign returns by 15%-20%. More bonds also became eligible, so the whole flow cannot be assigned to tax relief alone. The combination of after-tax carry and fewer ownership constraints distinguished India from markets relying mainly on defensive rate rises.

Russia's domestic borrowing challenge came from fiscal spending rather than an imminent external rollover. Sanctions have largely shut foreign markets, and defense spending was estimated to exceed the original budget by 4-5 trillion rubles, or $55-$69 billion. The deficit reached 6 trillion rubles, 2.6% of GDP, in the first five months—about 60% above the full-year target—and the 2026 debt ceiling had already been reached. Bloomberg Economics estimated that interest payments over the next decade would total at least 15% of GDP, roughly equal to the current public-debt stock. Low starting debt offered limited comfort when new financing was captive and expensive.

EMB rose 0.47% despite a stronger dollar. The fund's gain sat beside rising Indonesian bond yields, a slipping Philippine peso and Brazil's negative market response, underscoring the variety of local outcomes.

## Oil Ships Begin Moving, Though Prices and Assets Still Diverge

WTI slipped 0.25% to $76.60 while Brent rose 0.38% to $79.85. Both were far lower than a week earlier, by 12.67% and 11.65%, respectively. Kuwait planned to lift output above 2 million barrels a day within a week. Ships carrying nearly 10 million barrels had moved into or out of Hormuz, but damaged infrastructure and stranded volumes still put limits on how quickly supply could normalize. The physical news mattered more to the Treasury inflation debate than either small daily oil-price change alone.

The S&P 500 rose 1.08%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 2.48% and semiconductors jumped 6.42%, while VIX fell 11.06% to 16.40. Equities responded favorably to the prospect of cheaper energy and ongoing investment in technology. The same investment cycle, however, will bring more corporate borrowing and public power-infrastructure supply.

The dollar index rose 0.76% to 100.85, extending the response to the Fed's projections. Gold fell 3.09% to $4,224.10 as expected short rates rose and immediate geopolitical concern eased. Stronger equities and a stronger dollar coexisted: the former favored energy relief, while the latter continued to reflect a higher US policy path.

## The Holiday Leaves a Busy Week of Data and Supply

The US fixed-income market closes for Juneteenth on June 19. Trading resumes June 22 alongside $89 billion of 13-week and $77 billion of 26-week bill supply. Treasury then sells $69 billion of 2-year notes June 23, $70 billion of 5-year notes June 24 and $44 billion of 7-year notes June 25. The auctions will show whether demand for coupon and real-rate exposure remains as firm as Thursday's TIPS bidding when a larger calendar arrives.

Personal Income and Outlays is due June 25, with consensus calling for monthly PCE inflation of 0.5% headline and 0.3% core. Claims, durable goods and a GDP revision arrive the same morning. After Warsh's first meeting, those numbers will help settle whether lower spot energy is reaching measured prices while demand remains strong.

China's loan prime rate fixing and Canada's May CPI are due June 22; Australia's monthly CPI follows June 24. China is expected to hold 1- and 5-year LPRs at 3.00% and 3.50%. Canada's updated basket is expected to show headline inflation rising to 3.0% from 2.8%; Australia's previous monthly and annual readings were 0.4% and 4.2%. These releases will give a wider view of energy pass-through outside the US.

Colombia's presidential runoff on June 21 also precedes Banco de Mexico's June 25 decision, where a hold at 6.50% is expected. Peso and Colombian bond-market reactions will matter more than broad EMB performance for judging those local policy and fiscal risks.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries recover beyond the front end as oil ships cross Hormuz
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Oil began moving through the Strait of Hormuz under the interim US-Iran agreement. Brent was little changed on the day, but the physical shipments helped lower longer-term inflation concern. The five-year Treasury yield fell 4 basis points to 4.23%, and the ten- and 30-year each fell 3; the two-year declined just 1 basis point to 4.19%, retaining almost all of Wednesday's rise. A $24 billion five-year TIPS reopening drew 2.61 times coverage, with dealers receiving only 3.43%.

US labor and factory data offered no clear relief from the Fed's inflation concerns. Initial claims fell to 226,000, while continuing claims increased, and the Philadelphia Fed's prices-paid index rose to 53.2. Investors still priced a full quarter-point hike by October. Equity markets rose and volatility fell, but the dollar strengthened as the higher US policy path remained in view.

The Bank of England held at 3.75% in a 7-2 vote, while Indonesia and the Philippines each raised rates by 25 basis points. In credit, NextEra hybrids found buyers even with a tight premium, while Shutterfly offered 12.5% and other stressed borrowers faced discounts or creditor resistance. Proposed SpaceX financing could add at least $20 billion of investment-grade supply. The improved broad market did not give every borrower the same terms.
overall_summary.summary: Ships carrying nearly 10 million barrels moved through Hormuz, and strong demand at a $24 billion TIPS reopening supported bonds. The two-year yield barely fell after Wednesday's Fed-driven jump.
